findings.text: The unlock operation releases a mutex owned by the caller, preferring an uncontended path when build options permit and otherwise coordinating waiter wakeup through a sleepable path.

The lock operation acquires a mutex in uninterruptible sleep with default subclassing, combining dependency tracking with the realtime acquisition primitive and balancing tracking on success or failure.
Unlock serves as a schedulable entry that dispatches between immediate ownership clearing and contended transfer based on configuration and runtime contention state.
Lock serves as a schedulable entry that may sleep, delegating to immediate acquisition with fallback to ordered blocking when the lock is held.

A dedicated wait spinlock guards waiter membership, ordering, and waiter presence indication for both queue and tree based locks, and is required for insertion, removal, acquisition decisions, and indication maintenance.
Priority inheritance state of a task is guarded by its inheritance spinlock when clearing blocked designation and when linking the highest waiter for boosting during acquisition.

Contended release acquires interrupt saved wait serialization then current donation serialization then nested successor or donor donation serialization under disabled preemption, preserving a stable donation snapshot across release and transfer.

Ownership publication requires acquire visibility and release requires release visibility, with explicit barriers ensuring waiter insertion is visible before holder wounding and optimistic waiter marking is visible to concurrent fast observers.

Plain ownership pairs task identity with waiter presence, directed transfer, and pickup readiness markers; only the owner may release, clearing identity while retaining coordination markers, while directed transfer installs the successor and signals pickup.

Realtime ownership pairs task identity with a waiter presence marker that diverts concurrent modifiers to the serialized path; the marker is asserted optimistically before ownership checks and removed only after confirming no waiters remain.

Waiters carrying acquisition contexts are ordered by stamp with contextless waiters skipped to prevent starvation; one mode fails the requester when an older waiter exists and fails younger waiters, while the other mode orders by stamp and wounds a younger holder after queueing.

Waiter precedence follows increasing priority value with deadline ordering for deadline priorities; acquisition normally requires holding top precedence, with preemption by strictly higher precedence and narrowly allowed equal precedence preemption in spinlock builds that excludes realtime and deadline tasks.

Nonblocking acquisition succeeds only absent an owner and, when waiters exist, only when precedence rules allow preemption; one build always diverts through a locked slow try that can still acquire an idle lock, keeping behavior equivalent.

Optimistic waiter marking is repaired on every exit that does not leave waiters queued, preserving the equivalence that queued waiters imply the presence marker and avoiding spurious slow path diversion.

Validation of lock identity on release and of waiter linkage on wakeup is active only when global debug state enables it; otherwise those validations compile away and an immediate release path becomes available.
Slow entry, immediate win after entry, blocked win, deadlock handling, and presence of queued wakeups are reported through conditional counters that vanish when collection is disabled.

Plain locks anchor waiters in a doubly linked sequence supporting stamp ordered insertion and backward traversal from the tail, whereas realtime locks store waiters in a cached ordered tree supporting tail, head, insertion, and removal by node linkage.

Each waiter carries dual linkage for lock ordering and for inheritance boosting, with the top lock waiter linked into the new owner inheritance tree under inheritance serialization and validated to belong to the acquired lock.

Release moves among uncontended clearing, coordinated wakeup, and directed transfer states; waiter presence or explicit transfer marking selects coordination, proxy donation can force transfer, and successor wakeup occurs after serialization is dropped.

Slow acquisition moves among immediate retry, ordered blocking with contention observation, successful ownership, and failure cleanup with waiter removal and deadlock handling; waiter indication is reconciled before returning regardless of outcome.

Clearing waiter presence without holding serialization or without rechecking emptiness can resurrect a stale owner over a concurrent release; serialization plus presence recheck before clearing closes that window.

Donation state can change if preempted between inspection and serialization causing a missed transfer, early boot cannot assume interrupt control, and scheduling preparation must precede waiter queueing to avoid reentry through inheritance paths.
Waiter presence, directed transfer, pickup readiness, and realtime waiter presence markers form part of the ownership encoding contract and govern selection between immediate and coordinated paths.
Default acquisition blocks uninterruptibly and restores running state on failure, while inheritance traversal during blocking is bounded by a minimum chain walk limit.
